query: Why do expense decline rates differ across departments?

per_column.name: asset_type
per_column.rationale: Type of asset (hardware/software/cloud/travel) plausibly drives whether an expense is declined; a candidate cause of the decline outcome. Also varies by department, but its primary role here is a spend-category treatment whose effect on decline can be attributed.

per_column.name: entry_origin
per_column.rationale: Manual vs auto-generated entry plausibly affects decline likelihood (manual entries more error-prone), a candidate cause of the outcome.

per_column.name: has_source_id
per_column.rationale: Presence of a source_id (linkage/provenance) plausibly affects both how an expense is entered/originated and whether it is declined; a common cause of process treatment and outcome.

per_column.name: processing_lag
per_column.rationale: Processing lag is downstream of both the entry process and the decline decision (declined items may not be processed; 'not_processed' overlaps with decline). Conditioning on it induces bias; it is an outcome-related effect, not a common cause.

per_column.name: vendor_brand
per_column.rationale: Vendor/brand plausibly influences both asset_type (treatment) and decline likelihood (approved-vendor policies), a common cause surfaced from the CI/description data.

per_column.name: department_function_type
per_column.rationale: A grouping/attribute of department, which is the explicit axis of variation named in the query. Plausibly causes both the type of spend (treatment) and the decline rate, but it is essentially a re-encoding of the department already named in the query.

per_column.name: is_travel_related
per_column.rationale: Largely a derivative of asset_type/spend category (travel_equipment). It sits on the path between asset_type treatment and decline rather than being a common cause; redundant/mediating.

per_column.name: is_new_asset_acquisition
per_column.rationale: Constant (true for all 500 rows). No variance means it can identify nothing; contributes no causal information.

judge.rationale: A treatment is present (asset_type/entry_origin as candidate causes of decline). Some genuinely surfaced confounders exist (vendor_brand, has_source_id) that plausibly cause both the spend/process treatment and the decline outcome and are NOT named in the query. However, the one confounder most directly tied to the query axis (department_function_type) is a re-encoding of 'department', already named. Several added columns are problematic: processing_lag is a collider tangled with the outcome, is_travel_related is a mediator/redundant with asset_type, and is_new_asset_acquisition is constant and uninformative. So the set only partially realises a proper causal-adjustment design, with moderate-to-weak confounder quality.
